chunks: Musa ibn al-Qasim from Ali ibn Ja'far from his brother Musa ibn Ja'far (peace be upon them both) said:

I asked him about the skins of the sacrificial animals, whether it is permissible for the one who sacrifices to make them into a skin bag (container). He said: 'It is not permissible for him to make them into a skin bag unless he gives their value in charity.'

And we have clarified that whoever does not find the sacrificial animal but finds its value, he leaves the value with the one who buys the animal for him, and that person slaughters on his behalf. And we mentioned the case of one who does not have the value, and what is obligatory upon him regarding fasting: three days during Hajj and seven when he returns to his family. And it is not permissible to fast the days of Tashriq even with choice (of timing).
This is indicated by what he narrated:

key_terms.أَيَّامُ التَّشْرِيقِ: The days of Tashriq (11th, 12th, 13th of Dhu al-Hijjah)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on using the skins of sacrificial animals as containers in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: Imam Musa al-Kazim clarifies that while the skin of the sacrificial animal can be repurposed as a container (jirab), it is impermissible unless the owner compensates by giving its value in charity, reflecting the principle of converting animal byproducts into charitable wealth. The narration further contextualizes the expiation (kaffarah) for those unable to afford a sacrifice, specifying the ten-day fast structure and explicitly permitting the inclusion of the Days of Tashriq, a point of scholarly discussion regarding whether these days are excluded from fasting.
